questions.question: Which ruler of Vijayanagar allowed the Portuguese to build a church in his empire?
questions.solution: Venkatapati Raya was the younger brother of Sriranga Deva Raya and the ruler of Vijayanagara Empire with bases in Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore. His reign of three decades saw a revival of the strength and prosperity of the empire. He allowed the Portuguese to build a church in his empire.

questions.question: In whose reign, the office of the Vakil was abolished?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaha Jahan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vakil** was the **royal deputy**. It was a post filled only twice under the **seven great Mughal emperors.**
 
• At the end of Akbar’s reign, the office of Vakil became ‘more or less honorific’ and continued till the reign of **Shah Jahan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbar**

 
 
• He reformed and strengthened his central administration and also centralized his financial system and homeithe tax-collection procedures.
 
• Though he never renounced Islam, he took an active interest in other religions, motivating Hindus, Zoroastrians and Christians as well as Muslims, to engage in religious discussions before him.
 
• Illiterate himself, he encouraged scholars, poets, painters and musicians, making his court the center of culture. 
 
 
 
• **Jahangir**
 
 
• **Jahangir** was a ruler interested in** literature, music, painting and architecture.**
 
• During his reign, British officers **William Hawkins and Sir Tomas Rowe** appeared in the Mughal court.
 
• Jahangir wrote his autobiography titled** 'Tujuk-e-Jahangiri'. **
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**​
 
 
• **Aurangzeb** was a ruler of **Mughal dynasty**.
 
• He was the son of Shah Jahan.
 
• He died in the year 1707.
 
• He imposed Jizya, a military tax on non-Muslims who were not fighting for Mughal Empire.
 
• He was succeeded by his son Bahadur Shah I.
 
• Aurangzeb was also known as** 'Zinda Pir' **because of his simple lifestyle.

questions.question: After which of the following centuries, did the practice of donating land in South India go a long way?
questions.solution:

• Brahmadeya or the practice of donating land in the form of a whole village or a single plot to a Brahmin was prevalent till the early medieval period, i.e. until the 8th century.
 
• The practice was first started in South India in the 3-4th century AD.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers started the Mughal style of painting?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Mughal style of painting was started by the second Mughal Emperor **Humayun.**__
 
• He brought along with him 2 eminent Persian artists - Abd al-Samad and Mir Sayyed Ali when he returned from his exile. Based on his instructions, these artists created many paintings which were different from the traditional Persian art. Hence, a new style of art was born which was called ‘Mughal Painting’.

questions.question: What did the term 'bhoga’ refer to during the medieval period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**revenue assignments.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhoga**:-

 
 
• It was a term used in medieval India to refer to the revenue assignments made by the state to its officials and other beneficiaries.
 
• These assignments were usually in the form of land or other resources, which could be used for agricultural or other purposes.
 
• The term bhoga was also used to refer to the income generated from such assignments, which could be in the form of taxes, rents, or other forms of payment.
 
 
 
• **Revenue assignments:-**
 
 
• These were a crucial part of the feudal system that existed in medieval India, where the state granted land and other resources to its officials and other beneficiaries in exchange for their loyalty and service.
 
• These assignments were often hereditary and could be passed down from generation to generation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Donations to temples:- **

 
 
• These were also common during the medieval period, but they were usually made by individuals or groups rather than the state. These donations could take the form of money, land, or other resources, and were often made as a way of earning religious merit or gaining social status.
 
 
 
• **Festival**:-
 
 
• Festivals and religious functions were important parts of medieval Indian society, but they were not directly related to the system of revenue assignments.
 
• It could also be referred to as bhoga in some contexts, but these were not the primary meanings of the term during the medieval period.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri (or Jahangirnama**

__
 
• **Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri or Jahangir-nama** is the **autobiography** **of** Mughal Emperor Nur-ud-din Muhammad **Jahangir** (1569–1627).
 
• It is written in **Persian** and follows the tradition of his great-grandfather, **Babur** (1487–1530), who had written the **Baburnama**. 
 
• The autobiography is a unique piece of literature that shows his power of expression and observation. 
 
• In it, he not only provided the history of his reign but also gave details viz. his perception of art, politics, and also information about his family.
 
• The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is the most important sourcebook for the reconstruction of the history of the Mughal empire in the reign of Jahangir.
 
• Jahangir twice mentions a tower, tank, and pavilion used as a hunting palace about 29 km from Lahore.
 
• Tuzuk is also a very important source for the history of the Mughal expansion in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Akbar (1542-1605)**

 
• Akbar was one of the most successful emperors during the Mughal Era.
 
• He was born on October **1542** and died on 27th October **1605**.
 
• In **1555**, Humayan died just months after retaking Delhi. Akbar ascended the Mughal throne at the **age of 13 and became Shahanshah ("King of Kings")**. 
 
• His regent was **Bayram Khan**, his **childhood guardian**, and an outstanding warrior/statesman.
 
• In his court, there were nine jewels known as Navratan they were:
 
 
• Birbal: Administrator
 
• Abul Fazal: Scholar and statesman
 
• Faizi: Scholar and Statesman
 
• Todarmal: Finance minister
 
• Bhagwandas: Mansabdar
 
• Man Singh: Mansabdar
 
• Tansen: Musician
 
• Abdul Rahim khan-i-khana: Statesman
 
• Mulla do Pyaza
 
 

​Babar (1**526-1530**)

 
• ​Babur is the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• His original name was **Zahiruddin Muhammad.**
 
• Baburnama, also known as **Tuzk-e Babri** is a biography of Babur written by him.
 
• **Humayun** was the **son of Babur.**

**Aurangzeb** **(1658-1707)**

 
• Aurangzeb was the sixth, and widely considered the last effective Mughal Emperor. 
 
• He was crowned at Delhi under the title Alamgir.
 
• He captured Guru Teg Bahadur, the 9th Guru of Sikhs in 1675 AD and executed him when he refused to embrace Islam.
 
• He built the Bibi ka Maqbara, Moti Masjid, and Badshahi Mosque.

questions.question: Which of the following tax was initiated by the Alauddin Khilji?
questions.solution:
• Ghari was initiated by the Alauddin Khilji. Ghari was a house tax which was imposed by him on the people of his reign.
 
• Kharaj was a tax imposed by Firozshah Tughlaq on total production of lands which belonged to Non - Muslims.
 
• Zakat was a religious tax which was imposed on Muslims.
 
• In Kankut, the entire land was measured by pacing it and the crops were roughly calculated by inspection.
